newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold firms, volume surges on demand.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold firms, volume surges on demand.

text.p: Trade on the Istanbul gold exchange picked up on Monday, with volume leaping to 1,240 kilos from Friday's 594 kilos on physical demand from the free market, dealers said.
Gold closed firmer at $349.00 an ounce and 1,533,300 lira per gram, versus $347.50 and 1,516,900 on Friday, following higher prices in world markets.

"Today's trade was largely due to physical demand coming from the free market, but in the afternoon there was also some buying by banks taking up positons on gold's continued upward movement," one dealer said.
The Turkish lira closed weaker at 136,450 to the dollar after 136,130 on Friday, as the dollar strengthened against the mark.
Most of the day's trade -- 980 kilos -- took place in the morning session and 60.5 percent of the total was traded in lira terms. --Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
